Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Voltara Motors Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question at that time, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. If you're using a speakerphone, please pick up your handset before pressing the keys. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Voltara Motors' Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Elena Vasquez, CEO; Marcus Hale, CFO; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by these statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Elena Vasquez.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Q3 2024 was a pivotal quarter for Voltara Motors. We made significant strides in key areas, including our raw material sourcing and cost management strategies that shielded our margins amid volatility, record delivery volumes across models and regions that outpaced industry growth, aggressive cost reduction initiatives delivering billions in savings, and substantial electric vehicle range improvements coupled with efficiency gains that enhanced our competitive edge. We are particularly excited about the upcoming full ramp of the Voltara Ultra hyper-SUV and its anticipated boost to our profitability and market share in the premium segment.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Marcus Hale to discuss our financial performance in more detail.

Marcus Hale:
Thank you, Elena. Good morning, everyone. For Q3 2024, our revenue reached $12.8 billion, representing a 35% increase year-over-year, driven by our record deliveries and favorable mix shifts. Our gross margin expanded to 28.5%, reflecting the impact of our cost discipline, while operating expenses came in at $2.9 billion. Net income stood at $1.45 billion. We are maintaining a strong balance sheet with $18.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents. Our guidance for Q4 calls for revenue of $14.5 to $15.5 billion, with deliveries in the 260,000 to 280,000 range and continued gross margin expansion toward 32%.

As we dive deeper into our Q3 results, I'd like to highlight one of our key operational pillars: raw material sourcing and cost management. In the EV industry, battery metals account for upwards of 45% of our cost of goods sold—far higher than the 10-15% for traditional internal combustion engine vehicles—so this area forms a critical competitive advantage. Even with global lithium carbonate spot prices down 75% from their 2022 peak of $80,000 per metric ton, volatility persists due to surging demand from innovations like Tesla's 4680 cells and BYD's dominance in LFP batteries. Our disciplined strategy has protected our margins and set us up for the ramp at our Nevada Gigafactory.

On the numbers, our raw materials basket cost per vehicle dropped 18% year-over-year and 7% quarter-over-quarter, contributing to a 220 basis point gross margin expansion to 28.5%. Battery cell costs, which make up 35% of COGS, declined to $85 per kWh from $112 per kWh last year, aided by shifting to lower-cost LFP chemistries—now 55% of our pack production compared to 30% a year ago—and optimized NMC blends. Total critical minerals procurement came to $2.8 billion, flat sequentially but 12% below prior-year levels, even as our battery production rose 25% year-over-year to a 450 GWh annualized run rate.

Our sourcing approach balances supply security and cost control. We've secured 65% of our 2024-2026 needs for lithium, nickel, and cobalt through long-term offtake agreements, up from 45% at the start of last year. Highlights include our expanded partnership with Albemarle for 40,000 metric tons of spodumene concentrate annually from their Greenbushes mine in Australia, priced at index-linked levels capped at LME nickel benchmarks plus a 15% premium. For nickel, we've moved away from Indonesia's HPAL constraints—where delays at Tsingshan have idled 20% of capacity—sourcing 30% from low-carbon suppliers like BHP in Western Australia and Talon Metals' Tamarack project in Minnesota. Cobalt now represents just 8% of our cathode mix, thanks to NMC 811 optimizations and Umicore recycling partnerships, which help counter DRC-related geopolitical risks that drove premiums up 40% earlier this year.

Regionally, we're executing aggressively. In North America, 70% of our packs meet IRA compliance, qualifying for the full $45 per kWh production credit and $7,500 consumer incentives, vital as we scale platforms similar to GM's Ultium joint venture. Europe faces challenges from upcoming EU CBAM tariffs on Chinese graphite, so we've redirected 25% of anode material to synthetic graphite from Northern Graphite's Bissett mine in Canada, dodging disruptions at Syrah Resources in Mozambique. In China, which still dominates 60% of global cell production through CATL and EVE Energy, we've tapped cost advantages like $65 per kWh LFP from our Shanghai joint venture but limited it to 40% of volume to manage IP and tariff risks.

Beyond procurement, our cost management includes engineering innovations under our Battery 2.0 roadmap. We're vertically integrating precursor cathode active material production at our South Carolina facility, cutting intermediary markups by 22% with 98% yield rates. Our closed-loop recycling with Redwood Materials recovers 95% of lithium, nickel, and cobalt from end-of-life packs; Q3 intake hit 15,000 tons—covering 10% of virgin needs—with processing at $2.50 per kg versus market rates over $4. We're piloting silicon-dominant anodes for 15% higher energy density and 30% less graphite, sodium-ion for entry-level LFP packs targeting $50 per kWh by 2026, and Tesla-licensed dry electrode coating that slashes solvent costs 40% and enables thinner electrodes with lower CapEx.

Financially, we've hedged 50% of 2024 nickel exposure via LME futures at $18,000 per ton, cushioning a recent 15% rally from warehouse squeezes. Supplier programs reduced defect rates to 45 PPM from 120 year-over-year, saving $150 million in scrap and rework. This puts us ahead: peers reported higher inflation, like Ford's 8% and Rivian's 12%. We expect another 15% basket cost cut in FY24, supporting 32% margins at 800,000 units. Risks like Red Sea disruptions adding 5-10% to freight are offset by shifting 80% of high-value cells to air and rail.

Turning now to our delivery performance, we achieved a record 248,700 vehicles in Q3, up 28% year-over-year and 12% sequentially from Q2. This extends our streak of 11 straight quarters of growth, powered by ramps at our Gigafactories in Texas, Shanghai, and Berlin, plus mix shifts to higher-margin SUVs and trucks. Average selling prices held at $48,500, up 3% quarter-over-quarter from regulatory credits and premium features like Enhanced Autopilot.

By model, demand was broad-based. The Voltara Model S sedan, our high-volume entry comparable to Tesla's Model 3, delivered 102,400 units or 41% of total, up 32% year-over-year. The new Long Range RWD with LFP offers over 450 miles EPA range at under $40,000 post-IRA, with Texas Line 5 averaging 8,500 weekly and inventory at 2.1 weeks supply.

The Voltara Apex SUV, our top seller rivaling Model Y and Rivian R1S, hit 118,200 units or 48% mix, up 26% year-over-year. The 7-seater Tri-Motor AWD with 4680 packs delivers 510 highway miles and 0-60 in 3.1 seconds; Europe grew 45% with Berlin at 5,000 per week, lifting margins 220 basis points.

Voltara Titan pickup, targeting F-150 Lightning and Cybertruck, reached 24,900 units or 10%, up 85% from ramp exit. The Max Tow with 800V and V2G tows 11,000 pounds; Texas Line 3 sustained 1,800 weekly, though rare earth magnet issues limited us—Q4 should exceed 30,000.

The new Voltara Ultra hyper-SUV, blending Lucid luxury and Taycan performance, delivered 3,200 units or 1%, up 120% quarter-over-quarter from Shanghai's pilot, with $120,000-plus ASP, active thermal management, and 800V SiC for 350 kW charging.

Geographically, deliveries were 59% North America at 146,700 up 35%, led by Apex and Model S; IRA credits fueled Hertz and Amazon fleets adding 15,000, with Canada up 50% and Titan offsetting retail softness at $52,000 ASP. China took 21% or 52,200 up 18%, Model S and Apex strong despite BYD wars; 90% localization and 5,000 Ultra backlog. Europe 14% or 34,800 up 22%, Apex at 18,000 with German subsidies and Berlin doubling to 12,000 monthly; UK RHD Model S at 4,000, CBAM headwinds addressed by local 4680. APAC ex-China 5% or 12,400 up 45%, Apex in Japan/Australia; RoW 1% or 2,600 up 60% with UAE Titan and Mexico preps.

September accelerated 15% month-over-month, outpacing global EV sales growth per EV Volumes and gaining 1.2 share points to 4.8%. China price cuts pressured ASPs by 8% on Model S, offset by 25% FSD take-rate and $1.2 billion credits. 4680 at 65% mix cut $/kWh to $85, gigacastings trimmed Apex costs 30%, OTA updates lifted resale 12%. Q4 guidance 260,000-280,000 with Berlin and Titan expansions; vertical integration buffers EU subsidies and US tariffs for 30% FY25 growth.

Building on this momentum, our cost reduction initiatives have proven highly effective, delivering over $4.2 billion in annualized savings year-to-date. This drove vehicle COGS down 18% to $31,500 per unit on the core Apex platform, expanding gross margins 620 basis points to 23.8% and positioning us for 12% adjusted EBITDA margins in FY24, ahead of expectations amid demand softness, material swings, and Chinese competition.

Supply chain leads: batteries at 35-40% of BoM shifted 65% to LFP in Nevada, dropping cells 28% to $82 per kWh from $115, tracking global 22% deflation. Fixed contracts cover 80% cathode/anode to 2026. Europe localization at Hungary gigafactory avoids $1,200 duties per vehicle, widening spreads 15%; China JV leverages Apex Lite volumes for 12% deflation against BYD's sub-$10,000 Seagull.

Manufacturing next: gigacasting reduces underbody parts from 70 to one 9-meter piece, cutting assembly 42% and waste 30%, with 800V integration. Texas rates hit 1.2 vehicles/hour, saving $2,800 labor/overhead; Siemens AI maintenance cuts downtime 25%, OEE to 92%. 48V mild-hybrid trims high-voltage needs 20%.

Overhead down 14% to 7.2% of revenue via zero-based budgeting, 22% non-core headcount cut, 15% US dealer consolidation improving turns to 32 days and freeing $1.1 billion capital.

Effectiveness shows in 450 basis points structural expansion despite 9% ASP compression; sequential COGS fell 3% to $24,200 BoM, lowest in premium EV ahead of Lucid, matching VW ID.4. ROIC up to 18% from 9%. FY25 targets 12-15% more cuts at $70/kWh with Mexico 300,000 capacity, 80% gigacasting; Group14 synthetic anodes hedge graphite risks.

Finally, our electric vehicle range improvements and efficiency gains underscore our leadership. Flagship Model S hit 452 miles EPA, up 18% year-over-year, with Gen-3 120 kWh LFP/NMC at 280 Wh/kg topping Tesla's 4680. TerraSUV—our crossover—at 415 miles, 15% up, with 2.1 mi/kWh real-world or 476 Wh/mi from 500 beta vehicles.

This cut COGS 12% to $28,500, batteries to $78/kWh below $95 industry average, lifting EV margins to 28.5% despite 35% Reno ramp. PrismCell cylinders with silicon anodes reach 850 Wh/L, 800V for 350 kW charging adding 200 miles in 15 minutes; dry electrodes improve yield to 97%, eyeing $60/kWh in 2025.

Powertrain recaptures 85% regen via SiC inverters at 99% efficiency; thermal keeps cells under 35°C, degradation <1.5% at 100,000 miles. Aerodynamics at 0.198 Cd with shutters, panels, cameras; gigacastings drop weight 150 kg, Michelin tires Crr 0.0065 add 5%.

North America 75% IRA content unlocked $7,500 credits, 42% delivery growth to 65,000, NPS 92. Europe WLTP 720 km aids CO2 rules, 8% premium share; Northvolt sourcing 15% under spot. China 2.3 mi/kWh edges BYD, 28% growth at ¥289,000 ASP.

Roadmap to 500 miles by 2026 with QuantumScape solid-state at 400 Wh/kg; $1.2 billion R&D yields 15% conversion per 10% range gain, $0.03/mi savings vs. gas. Q4 OTA adds 20% efficiency for 3% Wh/mi cut, 25-30% deliveries, 30%+ margins.

Now, I'll hand the call back to the operator for the Q&A session.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one. Our first question comes from Jordan Lee at Goldman Sachs.

Analyst 1:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Marcus, on deliveries, China growth slowed to 18%—how are you navigating the price wars there, and what's the risk to ASPs if BYD cuts further?

Marcus Hale:
Thanks, Jordan. Solid question. In China, our 52,200 deliveries were led by Model S and Apex, holding 4% share despite the intensity. We've localized 90% via Shanghai, keeping competitive on NEV credits and made-in-China perks versus Xiaomi. ASP held firm thanks to Ultra backlog and FSD options. If cuts deepen, our cost deflation—12% YoY on platforms—lets us respond without margin erosion, targeting defense in APAC while prioritizing NA/Europe growth.

Operator:
Our next question from Emily Chen at Morgan Stanley.

Analyst 2:
Hi team, great results. Elena, on raw materials, with lithium deficits looming, how does your offtake and recycling stack up against peers, and any updates on the minerals venture fund?

Elena Vasquez:
Thanks, Emily. Our 65% lock-in for key metals, plus Albemarle and BHP deals, gives us security peers envy—our inflation was just 2% versus Ford's 8%. Recycling covers 10% needs at low cost, and the $5 billion fund stakes in Piedmont and Sigma secure supply. We're resilient for deficits, with hedges and low-cobalt shifts.

Operator:
Next from David Patel at JPMorgan.

Analyst 3:
Marcus, impressive range gains to 452 miles—can you elaborate on silicon anodes and thermal management impact on warranty costs, and Q4 efficiency guide?

Marcus Hale:
Absolutely, David. Silicon-dominant anodes boost density 14%, paired with liquid cooling holding temps below 35°C for half-industry degradation. Warranty benefits are clear: under 1.5% loss at 100k miles lowers claims 20%. Q4 OTA and regen tweaks target 20% gains, supporting margins.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your questions. We have time for one more.

Operator:
Our final question from Lisa Wong at Barclays.

Analyst 4:
Thanks. On cost reductions, the gigacasting rollout sounds game-changing—quantify the savings versus Tesla, and Mexico plant timeline?

Marcus Hale:
Lisa, gigacasting cuts parts 40%, assembly 42%, saving $2,800/unit at Texas—on par with Tesla but integrated with our 800V for extra efficiency. OEE at 92% amplifies it. Mexico ramps H1 2025 to 300k capacity, adding 12-15% COGS cuts via scale.

Operator:
Thank you. I would now like to turn the call back to Elena Vasquez for closing remarks.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, operator, and thank you all for joining us today. We are confident that Voltara Motors is well-positioned for continued success in the rapidly evolving automotive landscape. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Voltara Motors Q3 2024 earnings call. You may now disconnect.
